page: Microsoft Azure D160als_v7 is a compute-focused virtual machine from the Dalsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 160 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 80 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at a base speed of 4.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes advanced vector extensions such as AVX-512 and AVX_VNNI, alongside cryptography accelerators like AES and SHA_NI. The instance is configured with 320.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, though it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark results place this server in the top tier (top 10%) for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance, as measured by stress-ng and Geekbench. The AMD EPYC processor delivers high-throughput capabilities, achieving top-tier results in software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing. Memory bandwidth is also highly rated, with small-block cached reads reaching 14528.43 GB/sec and large-block uncached reads at 463.81 GB/sec. For database operations and key-value stores, the system processed 202.7 million Redis SET operations per second, placing it in the top 10% of tested hardware.

The primary tradeoff of the D160als_v7 is its resource density profile. While it offers massive parallel processing power with 160 vCPUs, the allocation of 2.0 GB of RAM per core limits its suitability for memory-bound workloads. However, this configuration provides high qualitative cost efficiency for compute-heavy tasks that do not require large memory footprints. The server is well-suited for CPU-bound workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, text processing, and large-scale LLM inference, where it demonstrates strong to top-tier token generation speeds.
